newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik ministry commander takes Dushanbe district.
newsitem.headline: Tajik ministry commander takes Dushanbe district.

text.p: Forces of Tajikistan's interior ministry commander, Sukhrob Kasimov, on Sunday seized a northern district of the capital from a rival warlord, witnesses said.

A Reuter correspondent saw jubilant fighters in green bandanas and waving automatic rifles tearing around the district in private cars and on the backs of army trucks. Fighting which had broken out the day before had stopped.
The Central Asian state has remained tense despite an agreement between the government and armed Islamic opposition in June, ending a four-year civil war which killed tens of thousands of people.

Fighting broke out on Saturday between Kasimov and forces loyal to senior tax official Yakub Salimov in a row over the killing of Kasimov's uncle earlier this week. But Western diplomats in the city said underlying the dispute was a battle for turf involving political and economic interests.
There was no word on casualties, but the International Committee of the Red Cross said on Saturday it had supplied a Dushanbe hospital with medicines to treat 40 injured people.
Salimov's whereabouts were unclear and Dushanbe was quiet but extremely tense, with few civilians on the streets and no private traffic in sight.

There was no visible sign of security being stepped up immediately around President Imomali Rakhmonov's palace, but peacekeepers from a Commonwealth of Independent States force had set up a check-point a few hundred metres (yards) away, between the palace and the contested northern district.
Tajikistan, which borders Afghanistan and China, is a former Soviet republic which gained independence after the superpower collapsed in 1991.
